A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same research work. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching content across the method renaming and document reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original federated-learning comparisons on four datasets, component and query ablations, feature visualizations, and three-seed CIFAR-10 results in its appendix.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, expanded uncertainty reporting, component and query ablations, and class-specific attention visualizations across the main text and appendix.

M1.justification: The shared ETF, LADM, BCE, and two-regularizer design remains. However, v3 Equation 12 excludes a negative feature's own prototype, whereas v1 Equation 7 includes all class prototypes. Per-sample label averaging is also made explicit. The expanded spatial-attention specification alone does not establish that the underlying implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both evaluate synthetic multi-label CIFAR-10 and DermaMNIST, PASCAL VOC, and ChestX-ray14 under the same eight label-skew settings. The new attention examples use existing DermaMNIST coverage; no dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added.

E2.justification: Tables 1–4 retain centralized training and the same six FL comparators: FedAvg, FedCurv, FedProx, SCAFFOLD, SphereFed, and FedLGT. FedMLP is newly discussed as related work but is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Tables 5 and 7 add ETF-classifier-only controls to the DermaMNIST and CIFAR-10 ablation designs. The main benchmark settings retain the same client participation, beta/gamma configurations, backbone, training budget, optimizer, and metrics. Renaming overall metrics as micro metrics does not establish a metric change.

E4.justification: New ETF-without-LADM rows test whether fixed prototypes suffice without disentanglement. New Figure 5 provides DermaMNIST attention-map case studies supporting class-specific localization. Existing loss/query ablations, t-SNE plots, and cosine-similarity analyses remain, including their appendix counterparts.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-seed means and standard deviations only for CIFAR-10 at beta=0.5 in appendix Table 9. v3 states three-seed repetition generally and reports mean plus standard deviation throughout main Tables 1–4, substantially broadening uncertainty reporting. This does not establish an increase beyond three runs for the previously replicated setting; ablation tables still omit uncertainties.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–4 extensively revise reported scores and some rankings. For CIFAR-10 at beta=0.1, macro-F1 leadership changes from SphereFed (39.52 versus 38.14) to the proposed method (38.09 versus 36.83). Even the previously three-seed CIFAR-10 beta=0.5 proposed macro-F1 changes from 49.17 in v1 Table 9 to 48.17 in v3 Table 1. New ablation rows and attention maps add findings; these revisions do not demonstrate a same-setting implementation improvement.

T1.justification: Equation 1 corrects the ETF construction from I_C - J_C/(C-1) to I_C - J_C/C, making it consistent with the stated simplex geometry and inner products. The NC properties remain substantively unchanged, and neither version provides new theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains NC-inspired feature disentanglement and alignment for multi-label label-skewed FL. The headline maximum gains change from 2.87% macro-AUC and 7.29% macro-F1 in v1's introduction/conclusion to 3.92% and 4.93% in v3's abstract/conclusion, without expanding the claimed task coverage.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges that the method does not lead in ChestX-ray14 micro-AUC and argues that its macro-AUC advantage indicates better minority-disease performance. It also adds explanations for ETF-only degradation and interprets the new attention maps as class-specific spatial selection. The existing clustering interpretation remains.

D1.justification: v3 documents spatial feature-map reshaping and fixed 2D positional encoding, specifies uniform model averaging in Algorithm 1, and assigns lambda1 explicitly to 1 for CIFAR-10 and 0.01 otherwise. v1 leaves these details absent or generic. These disclosures improve implementation specificity without establishing corresponding changes to earlier experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of FedMLP and positions LADM relative to DETR, while removing v1's specific criticism that MLC-NC does not address missing classes. The bibliography is unchanged, and new attributions contain unresolved citation placeholders. Existing heterogeneous-FL discussion is largely relocated to Appendix A.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the abstract, introduction, method exposition, and discussion are rewritten. FedNCAlign-ML becomes FedNCA-ML, sections and appendices gain numbering, the algorithm moves into the main method section, and detailed heterogeneous-FL related work moves to the appendix. This is extensive editorial restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redesigned to show label correlations and LADM internals, and Figure 5 adds attention maps. Main tables are reformatted for uncertainty reporting, with v1's appendix Table 9 incorporated into Table 1. Existing analytical plots are retained or relocated; captions and metric headers are also revised.

improvement.justification: Broader uncertainty reporting, ETF-only controls, clearer implementation details, and the corrected ETF formula strengthen support for the existing contribution. The net gain is limited by unresolved citation placeholders, uncertainty-free ablation tables, and new text–table inconsistencies: Section 5.3 claims a 1.21-point ChestX-ray14 macro-AUC margin at beta=0.1, whereas Table 4 gives 71.28 minus 70.16, or 1.12 points.
